key_terms.الأشنان: Potash or soapwort (ushnan) — a plant used for washing and cleaning, historically important as a cleaning agent before soap became widespread
key_terms.زكاة: Zakat — the obligatory religious alms-tax, one of the pillars of Islamic worship

ai.seo_question: Is there zakat on potash (ushnan) in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman reports asking Imam al-Kazim (peace be upon him) whether zakat is obligatory on potash (ushnan), a plant used for cleaning. The Imam gave a concise negative ruling: zakat is not required on it. This hadith is part of a chapter clarifying which items from vegetation and plants are exempt from the zakat obligation, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential principle that zakat applies only to specific enumerated items.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar and someone else, from Yunus who said,

en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ill ibn Marrar and others from Yunus who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if there is Zakat on saltwort.
He (the Imam) said, ‘No, Zakat is not due on it.’”
